name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Charged Pike CP-3 'Longreach'
description:
A 2.5-meter pike with an electrically charged spearhead that delivers a stunning discharge on penetration. The Longreach combines the oldest tactical principle in close combat — reach advantage — with modern electrical incapacitation. The carbon-lattice shaft is lightweight enough for rapid thrusting while rigid enough to resist lateral bending forces that would snap conventional materials, and the Ablonite-KR ceramic spearhead carries a capacitor charge that discharges on contact with conductive materials.

Arcturus developed the Charged Pike for corridor defense scenarios where security teams need to hold chokepoints against approaching threats without resorting to firearms. The weapon's 2.5-meter reach means defenders can engage targets before they reach striking distance, and the electrical discharge on the spearhead ensures that even glancing contact is incapacitating. Teams of three pike-armed operators can seal a standard corridor completely, presenting a wall of electrified points that no unarmored attacker can pass.

The CP-3's revival of the pike as a tactical weapon reflects a broader recognition in GLMZ's security culture that ancient formation weapons retain their effectiveness in the city's endless corridors and confined spaces. The geometry of indoor combat — narrow approaches, limited flanking, channeled movement — creates conditions identical to those that made the pike dominant on historical battlefields. Arcturus simply added electricity.
specifications:
total_length: 250 cm
weight: 1.8 kg
shaft_material: Carbon-lattice composite
spearhead_material: Ablonite-KR ceramic with embedded capacitor
discharge_voltage: 40,000 V on contact
power_source: Shaft-integrated capacitor, 80 discharges
head_length: 25 cm
tactical_use: The Longreach dominates corridor defense through reach and electrical threat. Three-person pike formations seal standard corridors against approaching threats, with each operator covering a third of the corridor width. The electrical discharge ensures that attackers who push past the spearpoint still receive an incapacitating shock. Against armored targets, the Ablonite-KR ceramic head penetrates composite armor through material hardness, and the discharge propagates through conductive armor components. The weapon's limitation is lateral mobility — the shaft's length makes it impractical in open spaces where attackers can flank.
cultural_context: The return of pike formations to GLMZ's security landscape has generated both practical respect and historical humor. Security teams who train with the CP-3 have studied historical pike drill manuals and adapted square-formation tactics to rectangular corridors. The aesthetic of armored security operators wielding electrified pikes in carbon-lattice corridors has been described as 'medieval neo-noir' — a label that the operators themselves find more accurate than ironic.
story_hooks: A pike formation was broken by an attacker who deployed a counter-weapon specifically designed to exploit the pike's lateral weakness — a short-range area-effect device that disrupted the formation without entering the pikes' reach. Someone studied the tactic and designed its counter.

An unauthorized pike formation has appeared in a lower-tier district, using homemade versions of the CP-3 to hold a corridor against all comers. The community behind the formation is protecting something — and corporate security cannot breach without casualties.

physical_description.visual_profile: A towering polearm with an aggressive forward profile—a sleek, tapering ceramic spearhead mounted on a nearly invisible carbon-lattice shaft that catches light like translucent crystal. The head dominates despite its modest 25cm length, appearing to float on air due to the shaft's extreme thinness relative to its 2.5-meter reach. At rest, it presents like a conductor's baton scaled to lethal proportions.
physical_description.dimensions: 250 cm total length, 25 cm spearhead length, 4.2 cm shaft diameter at widest grip section, narrowing to 2.1 cm at the coupling point
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light and perfectly balanced—1.8 kg distributes along the full length, eliminating the top-heavy feel of traditional pikes. Feels almost weightless in trained hands during slow movements, but the momentum builds with speed. Handles like a fencing foil scaled up, not a sledgehammer.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-lattice composite shaft (visible as subtle geometric tessellations under certain angles), Ablonite-KR ceramic spearhead (crystalline appearance)
physical_description.finish: Shaft: matte charcoal with micro-texturing for grip security, almost invisible until light strikes it at angles. Spearhead: high-gloss ceramic with faint amber undertones where the capacitor matrix is visible beneath translucent layers. Minimal surface treatment—function-forward aesthetic.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray shaft transitioning to pale amber/golden ceramic at the head. The spearhead's tip is knife-edge silver where the Ablonite-KR comes to its final point. Arcturus's chrome-silver manufacturer badge sits at the grip midpoint.
physical_description.grip_texture: Wrapped in carbonized grip tape with subtle cross-hatching—friction-optimized, slightly tacky to the touch, designed for gloved hands. The tape transitions from aggressive grip at the primary control section to smoother texture toward the butt end.
distinctive_features: Spearhead faceting creates visible crystalline geometry, suggesting internal capacitor architecture
Faint blue-green phosphorescence along spearhead edges (capacitor charge indicator—visible in low light)
Three equidistant micro-vents running down the shaft near the head (thermal dissipation for charge cycling)
Chrome Arcturus Defense Solutions emblem at grip, with serialized batch marking below
Tapered butt end with reinforced strike point (anti-personnel use possible)
Subtle wear patterns on spearhead facets suggest contact-scoring from previous discharges
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions chrome logo engraved at grip center, 3cm wide. Serial plate (2cm × 1cm) stamped below grip with batch number and discharge count meter. Model designation 'CP-3' stamped along the shaft in small sans-serif at the 100cm mark.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained and reliable. Spearhead shows light amber oxidation from repeated capacitor cycling. Grip tape worn smooth in the primary control area from regular use. No major damage typical—the weapon's design prioritizes durability. Operators keep the spearhead electrostatically clean.
